annotations.text: ROUND 2 — THE APP: BOOTH, AS PICKED. The original board from the first canvas, untouched — Barlow Condensed, 48px of chrome, abstract camera-feed tiles (no film footage anywhere in the app; the film's job ends at the landing page), lower-thirds, bounty rail. The accent chip above the frame is live — try the four colors. Right board is the same design reflowed to a day-one reality: one live room at full size, real bounties, and an OPEN A ROOM tile instead of dead placeholders. All room/pool data is sample.

BOOTH — THE APP. Verbatim port of the board you chose: the product is the interface, everything on screen is a room. This is what ENTER MEGACHAT on the landing routes into, same tab. The landing keeps its own skin (Archivo/mint) — marketing page and terminal looking different is the hyperliquid pattern, not a bug.

BOOTH — DAY ONE. Same language (type, chrome, mesh feeds, accent, rail), reflowed to what's actually live early on: one room at hero scale beats six half-dead tiles. The dashed OPEN A ROOM tile is the empty state doing sales work. If this board holds up, Booth survives the cold start you flagged when we banked it.

LANDING V1 — the picked mix: B1's engineering skin (Archivo caps, mint accent, hard edges) carrying B3's content (the four feature rows, "a chat app for people who'd rather be on TV") plus the full reference-style scroll: stat row, live-rooms table, bounty board, how-a-seat-works.

The hero plays the REAL launch film once (compressed preview cut), holds its final frame with a soft dim, and the small circle bottom-right replays it. Headline reveals staged, with a sweep under BE THE STREAM.

Still open: final film's Shot B re-roll will replace the hero video; wordmark/logo placement (currently type-only, B1-style); real room/bounty data at launch.

ROUND 1.5 — B'S STRUCTURE, REBUILT ON THE REFERENCE SET. Every board keeps what won in B (full-bleed film hero, quiet chrome, dark ground, editorial restraint) and swaps the serif for a voice pulled from one reference: hyperliquid's engineering caps, ebisu's marquee-and-cards, fomo's heavy lowercase, fantasy.top's board-as-centerpiece. VERDICT: B1 took the style, B3 took the content — merged into Landing V1 (first page).

B1 · HYPERLIQUID CUT — engineering luxury: letterspaced caps nav, hard-edged mint CTA, a big-number mechanics row (all true product facts, no invented totals), and a live-rooms table styled like a price board.
Why: the most credible-with-money read; the table IS the product demo.
Tradeoff: coldest of the four — personality rides almost entirely on the film.
VERDICT: winner — style.

B2 · EBISU CUT — the on-brand one: gradient marquee strip up top, the M-mark in the nav, rounded film hero card, four mechanic cards (their Borrow/Leverage/Earn/Stake pattern), bounty strip, sticker lockup at the close.
Why: brand kit fully deployed inside a proven crypto-landing skeleton.
Tradeoff: busiest of the four — the most elements competing with the film.

B3 · FOMO CUT — heavy lowercase statement voice ("where fans become the show."), caps-kicker feature rows, dual pill CTAs, gradient spent on the headline's last two words.
Why: the most fun-digital register; reads consumer-social, not fintech.
Tradeoff: lowercase-everything is a whole personality — it commits the brand to casual forever.
VERDICT: winner — content (feature rows + closing statement, folded into Landing V1).

B4 · FANTASY CUT — the board is the centerpiece: bounty leaderboard with rank/pool/pledges/claim, gold accent, three role cards (fan / streamer / backer).
Why: game energy without comic chrome; gives the money mechanic top billing.
Tradeoff: leads with bounties over seats — a bet that the leaderboard, not the camera, is the hook.

ROUND 1 — THE LANDING PAGE, FOUR WAYS (record). B won on structure; A (Sticker Bomb) and D read vibe-coded, C hides the video. A's board was retired when its slot became the Landing V1 build — its brand-at-full-volume idea lives on in the asset kit. Round 1.5 refined B against the reference set; the merge lives on the Landing V1 page.

B · PRESTIGE BROADCAST — the film IS the identity. Full-bleed still, one cyan accent, zero logo images.
Why: the most premium read; nothing competes with the video.
Tradeoff: the serif voice read uppity/pretentious — structure won, type lost.
VERDICT: winning structure, refined in Round 1.5.

C · IMPACT COMIC — the cracked MEGA as the site's whole voice: halftone paper, hard shadows, the film retold as a three-panel strip.
Why: unforgettable, meme-native, real merch energy.
Tradeoff: buries the video; comic chrome is a hard register to trust with money.
VERDICT: cut for the landing — the smash graphics stay in the kit for stream-overlay moments.

D · SIGNAL GRID — the grown-up bridge: monochrome discipline, gradient spent only on the primary CTA.
Why: ages best, extends into app UI most directly.
Tradeoff: safest = least memorable.
VERDICT: cut (read as vibe-coded).
